title: Edge region capacity briefing + mitigation notes — 2026-04-12
content:
Context: Quick sync after the ops call. We ran two short pre-warming experiments last week and saw mixed wins depending on model family and seq len. This doc captures the regional capacity snapshot, a near-term hedging plan, and open action items for the week.

Summary points:
- Overall fleet healthy but tight at peak in three regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-northeast1) during evening PST spikes.
- Pre-warm experiment reduced cold-start tail latency by ~18% for short chats on c-model-3b but added 6% CPU/GPU overhead when idle retention configured at 5m.
- Hedge pool plan proposed: 10% spare GPUs in each major region + cross-region borrow window (30m) for unexpected surges.

Regional snapshot (observed 2026-04-09 -> 2026-04-11):
- us-west1: total GPUs provisioned 480, reserved for Dedicated 220, free pool 60 (after autoscale headroom), ephemeral pool 200. Peak utilization hit 87% Tue 19:00 PST.
- us-east1: total 360, reserved 160, free pool 50, ephemeral 150. Peak utilization 76%.
- eu-west1: total 200, reserved 80, free pool 20, ephemeral 100. Peak utilization 92% Wed 17:30 CEST (hot shard on retrieval-heavy workloads).
- ap-northeast1: total 80, reserved 30, free pool 5, ephemeral 45. Peak 89% Thu 02:00 JST.
- ap-south1: total 40, reserved 10, free pool 10, ephemeral 20. Peak 55%.

Observations / anomalies:
- eu-west1 sharp spike correlated with model-version rollout (m-v2.4) and a canary that accidentally had full KV caching enabled; caused KV memory pressure on a subset of instances.
- us-west1 night spike shows many short-lived inference bursts (token length < 40) where current batching window (20ms) may be suboptimal.
- ap-northeast1 low free-pool margin and higher 90th latency for embeddings; likely due to background multi-tenant reranking jobs.

Experiment notes (pre-warm A/B):
- A: aggressive pre-warm (keep-kv 5m, keep-warm instances x2) -> lower cold tail, +6% cost while idle, slightly higher OOM incidents on older driver builds.
- B: selective pre-warm (only for high-QPS routes, keep-kv 2m) -> 8–12% latency reduction for targeted routes, ~2% cost delta.
- Recommendation: roll selective pre-warm (B) in us-west1/us-east1 this week for chat-high routes; postpone eu-west1 until KV caching rollout is validated.

Hedging & routing policy proposal:
- Maintain 10% permanent spare in each region (from ephemeral pool). Marked as "hedge-reserve" and only used when cross-region borrow is active.
- Implement cross-region borrow window of 30 minutes with automatic de-escalation if latency > SLO. Borrowing should prefer same-continent peers first (us-west1 <-> us-east1 allowed with low weight penalty).
- Route by cost tier for internal low-priority batch jobs: send to ap-south1 or spare ephemeral pools during peak.

Immediate action items (owner - ETA):
- (Asha) Update autoscale policy to tag 10% hedge-reserve in us-west1 and eu-west1 - ETA 2026-04-14.
- (Marco) Reproduce KV caching OOM case in eu-west1 (test harness + driver 0.21) - ETA 2026-04-13.
- (Sophie) Implement selective pre-warm rollout for chat-high routes behind feature flag (canary 5%) - ETA 2026-04-15.
- (Jonah) Add dashboard panel for per-route free-pool headroom and cross-region borrow events - ETA 2026-04-14.
- (Oncall) Add temporary alert: free-pool < 8% sustained for 10m -> page infra-team until hedge-reserve activation.

Medium-term asks / considerations:
- Evaluate trimmed-precision quant kernels for embeddings on ap-northeast1 to reduce memory pressure; target proof-of-concept by end of Q2.
- Consider adding small regional spot pools (in partner clouds) for non-sensitive batch inference as a lower-cost overflow. Legal + procurement to assess.
- Revisit batching window heuristics: propose adaptive windowing based on observed short-token bursts (experiment design by eng-systems).

Risk register (short):
- Runaway canary enabling full KV caching -> region-wide memory pressure (mitigation: fail canary fast, rollback, targeted cache-evict).
- Cross-region borrow latency regressions affecting tail; plan to limit to burst-only and revert automatically.
- Cost drift from persistent pre-warm without ROI; weekly cost delta checks required.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally operational and contains quick numbers from last three days — treat as working briefing. Please add comments in the doc or ping in #fleet-ops for urgent blockers.
- If you want to test the pre-warm configs, use /infra/experiments/prewarm-2026-04 on the test harness; include reproduction steps in the jira ticket.

Appendix (quick links):
- prewarm experiment logs: gs://redwood-ops/experiments/prewarm/2026-04-09_logs
- hedging playbook draft: confluence.redwood/hedging-playbook-draft
- autoscale policy PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1142

End of briefing.
